records.finding: Attribute-limit comment claimed the SDK default would silently drop an outcome's ~12 attributes; sdk/log@v0.22.0 default attribute count limit is 128 (defaultAttrCntLim), so the default would NOT drop them. Rationale was false; the -1 setting itself is correct.
records.evidence: // SDK's default limit would silently drop them (a real sdk/log footgun, ADR-0002's experimental-dependency risk realized here).
records.reason: Rewrote to the true rationale: WithAttributeCountLimit(-1) removes the cap so field growth never silently truncates; the 128 default clears today's ~12 but is a silent cliff, and a directly built zero-value Record has limit 0.

records.finding: Shutdown returned only the metric-leg error when both legs failed, discarding the log-leg error (a flush failure that can mean dropped outcome data). Both Shutdowns ran (no leak) but the second error was swallowed.
records.evidence: if mErr != nil { return mErr }; return lErr
records.reason: Shutdown now returns errors.Join(mErr, lErr). Regression test TestShutdownJoinsBothErrors (both-fail, metric-only, event-only) asserts each leg's error surfaces via errors.Is and both legs always close.

records.finding: Reconstructed span context set only TraceID; TraceFlags left zero, so emitted outcome events carried an unset (unsampled) flag. Backends that gate log-to-trace correlation on the sampled flag may drop the linkage.
records.reason: Set TraceFlags: oteltrace.FlagsSampled on the SpanContextConfig. SpanID deliberately stays zero — an outcome references a transaction's trace, not a specific span; documented in the code comment.
